success_patterns: Six of eight successes had the clue reproduced verbatim or near-verbatim in the first passage (archive or flashcard text). The agent matched on distinctive words and answered directly with the entity the passages tie to the clue. This is already covered by Rule 3.

The agent named the answer slot before answering. 'This group's Adam Duritz' gave the band, not the singer. 'This British sculptor' gave the person. 'the 14th one of these spiritual leaders' gave the title. 'one of these bombs' gave the standard compound. 'flag seen here' gave the country. All of this is already covered by Rules 2 and 4 and the strategic guidance.

Passages named a nearby or related entity at the wrong level: the oil well Leduc No. 1 for a 'city ... Canada's oil capital' clue, or the band's albums and songs for a 'group' clue. The agent chose the entity whose level matched the clue's category noun and descriptors (city, group) and ignored the sub-entity (well, song). Only the film/song and team/city cases are covered so far.

Answers were bare and short (Edmonton, Max Factor, Counting Crows, Henry Moore, Dalai Lama, hydrogen bomb, ukulele, Cyprus). A single reasoning pass was enough when the answer type was fixed first and the passages repeated one entity alongside the clue's unique details. This is already covered.

patch.reasoning: Nearly every observed success is already covered by existing rules, so the only edit is a short ordered procedure placed at the top of the skill, as the optimizer memory recommends. It follows the order of use: slot type, verbatim scan, level/granularity check, bare form. It points back to the existing rules instead of adding new example bullets. The one new element is the granularity check, which is the Leduc-vs-Edmonton and song-vs-group trap seen in this batch. The edit is about six lines, so net length stays small and no existing rule is weakened.

edits.content:
## Quick procedure (apply in this order, one brief reasoning line before the answer tags)
1. SLOT TYPE: write the noun type the clue asks for (person / group / city / country / title / common noun / word). Pronouns and 'this/these/one of these <X>' fix the type. Anchors already named in the clue are never the answer.
2. VERBATIM SCAN (Rule 3): look for the clue's distinctive words repeated in any passage, with the answer next to them. Copy that answer's form.
3. LEVEL CHECK: passages often name a related entity at a different level (a well vs. the city, a song or album vs. the band, a member vs. the group, a region vs. the country). Choose the one that matches the clue's category noun and ALL its descriptors (e.g. 'city ... oil capital', 'group').
4. FORM: give the bare standard name (Rule 4 and Strategic guidance section 4).
